newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi power generation due to triple in 25 years.
newsitem.headline: Saudi power generation due to triple in 25 years.

text.p: Power generation in Saudi Arabia is due to increase by three times over the next 25 years, the kingdom's industry and electricity minister said in remarks published on Wednesday.

"As the electric sector expands in the next 25 years...(it) will basically, generation-wise, expand by three times," Hashem bin Abdullah bin Hashem Yamani said, as quoted by the Saudi daily Arab News.
The minister was speaking at the inauguration of a new high voltage cable production line in the western port city of Jeddah.
By the first quarter of 1996, actual Saudi power generation capacity had reached 19,000 megawatts, the paper said.
The government expects peak electricity consumption to reach 23,310 megawatts by the end of the decade from 17,228 MW in 1994/95.
To meet this demand, the government is planning to raise power generation capacity to 25,273 MW in 2000 from 18,238 in 1994/95.
Official statistics say the electrification rate stood at 83 percent of the population in 1994. Saudi Arabia's population hovers around 18 million.
Government figures show that 21 billion riyals ($5.6 billion) have been earmarked to boost power generation between 1995 and 2000 and an additional 27 billion riyals for distribution.
